office_does: A State Representative serves a two-year term writing and voting on Washington state law and the operating, capital and transportation budgets, covering school funding, tax structure, housing rules, health funding and criminal-justice statutes.
race_blurb: Republican Rep. Travis Couture, the House Republican budget leader since his 2023 arrival, faces first-time Democratic candidate Maria Littlesun, a Shelton social worker and tribal elder-care manager. He campaigns on spending control, public safety and I-1; she campaigns on social housing, special-education funding and reproductive-care access.

candidates.summary: House Republican budget leader since 2023, a Navy submarine veteran and Shelton construction-business owner running on lower costs, public safety and parental rights.
highlights: Voted against ESSB 6346 and offered amendments to delay the tax and cut a related sales tax on advertising services [S5][S6][S7]
As budget leader, proposes to 'control unsustainable spending' and 'reject unnecessary tax increases' [S2]
Campaigning for I-1: 'Vote yes for parents' rights and vote no for stranger danger' [S4]
Pledges to support law enforcement and 'hold repeat offenders accountable' [S2]

taxes.basis: Voted no on ESSB 6346, ESSB 5813 and ESHB 2081 and yes on I-2111; sponsored amendments to delay the income tax; campaigns for 'less taxes.'

spending.basis: Calls for controlling 'unsustainable spending' and eliminating waste; criticizes 'reckless spending.'

safety.basis: Supports law-enforcement staffing, repeat-offender accountability, restored pursuits and drug penalties, and encampment cleanup.

experience.basis: Incumbent since 2023 and House Republican budget leader; runs on 'experience ... and a record of results.'

social.basis: Voted against ESSB 5599 and ESHB 1469 (2023 reproductive and gender-affirming care bills); no I-638 position.

parental-rights.basis: Campaigns for I-1, says he drafted the current notification language, voted for I-2081 and against ESHB 1296, and supports school choice.

candidates.summary: First-time candidate from Shelton, a social worker and crisis responder who manages Squaxin Island Tribe elder and vulnerable-adult programs, running on affordability, housing, schools and healthcare.
highlights: Supports social housing with wraparound services and tenant protections; says encampment sweeps do not solve root causes [S5]
Would champion full special-education funding and restore dual-language program funding [S5]
Pledges to protect access to contraception and medical abortion [S5]
Wants to protect Apple Health/Medicaid and keep rural clinics open [S5]

spending.basis: Proposes added funding for special education, dual-language programs, rural transit and affordable-housing construction.

housing.basis: Backs social housing, tenant protections and affordable-housing funding, alongside zoning reform for density near transit.

safety.basis: Opposes encampment sweeps and favors social housing with wraparound behavioral-health services.

healthcare.basis: Wants to protect Apple Health and Medicaid access and reform insurance rules within the current system.

social.basis: Pledges to protect contraception and medical-abortion access; endorsed by Planned Parenthood Alliance Advocates and Stonewall Democrats.

experience.basis: First-time candidate with a social-services and tribal elder-care background.
